dependency_coverage.name: NumStability.HDP.Scalar.IndependentSums.Bernstein.SubExponentialLinearMGF
dependency_coverage.interpretation: Unfolds to the conjunction: Measurable X; 0 < K; Integrable X wrt mu; integral of X wrt mu equals 0; and for every real lam with |lam| <= 1/K, exp(lam * X) is mu-integrable and its integral satisfies E exp(lam X) <= exp(K^2 * lam^2). dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It is the sole hypothesis carrying the distributional class of each X i, and it is what fixes the numeric parameter K i that then appears in both denominators of the bound. It also silently supplies measurability, integrability and mean-zero, and it forces K i > 0, so it rules out the degenerate K = 0 case.

Printed page 32, Proposition 2.7.1 (e): 'E exp(lam X) <= exp(K_5^2 lam^2) for all lam such that |lam| <= 1/K_5', valid for mean-zero X and equivalent to properties (a)-(d), i.e. to sub-exponentiality; footnote 8 on printed page 36 states that (e) holds for a K_5 within an absolute constant factor of ||X||_psi_1. Sub-exponential is Definition 2.7.5 (printed page 33), i.e. finiteness of ||X||_psi_1 = inf{t > 0 : E exp(|X|/t) <= 2}.

Two deviations: (i) sub-exponentiality is replaced by the linear-MGF property of Proposition 2.7.1 (e) with an explicit per-index parameter, which is the source's own equivalent characterisation only up to an absolute constant factor (footnote 8, printed page 36), not Definition 2.7.5 itself; (ii) the hypothesis 0 < ∑ (a i * K i)^2 is added, which given K i > 0 is exactly a ≠ 0 and therefore narrows the printed 'a in R^N, arbitrary'. Deviation (ii) is a necessary repair, since the printed right-hand side divides by ||a||_2^2 and ||a||_inf and is not a well-defined real number at a = 0, but it is still an added side condition relative to the printed text, so this check cannot be recorded as a clean pass.

semantic_checklist.source_evidence: Single conclusion: P{|sum_{i=1}^{N} a_i X_i| >= t} <= 2 exp[- c min(t^2/(K^2||a||_2^2), t/(K||a||_inf))], where K = max_i ||X_i||_psi_1 (printed page 37).

semantic_checklist.reasoning: Every structural component of the printed conclusion is present and in the same arrangement: probability of a two-sided tail event on the left; prefactor 2 times a real exponential on the right; a negated product of the constant with a two-argument minimum in the exponent; the sub-gaussian (t^2) branch first and the sub-exponential (t) branch second. No conjunct, case or witness of the source conclusion is dropped. The identity of the two denominators is a separate question, handled under C06, C08 and C09.

K is defined in the statement as max_i ||X_i||_psi_1.

Instead: SubExponentialLinearMGF mu (X i) (K i) (an MGF predicate with parameter K i), the fused quantity ∑ i, (a i * K i)^2, and Finset.univ.sup' hne (fun i => |a i| * K i). Standard operators are interpreted correctly from their declarations: Measure.real = (mu s).toReal, GE.ge = flipped ≤, abs = max a (-a), Min.min = real minimum, Finset.sup' = maximum over a nonempty finset, HDiv = real division, iIndepFun = joint independence.

Reading this declaration one cannot recover the printed formula without invoking Proposition 2.7.1 and a rescaling argument.

semantic_checklist.source_evidence: Real-valued random variables, finitely many of them (indices 1, ..., N), real weight vector a in R^N, real threshold t >= 0.
semantic_checklist.lean_evidence: Scalar field ℝ throughout; index type an arbitrary Fintype with hne : Finset.univ.Nonempty; weights a : ι → ℝ unconstrained in sign or size; probability space arbitrary.
semantic_checklist.reasoning: No change of scalar field or dimension. Two identified changes of scope: (i) generalization from {1, ..., N} to an arbitrary nonempty finite index type and from a fixed probability space to an arbitrary one, both purely notational reindexings; (ii) a specialization of the printed hypothesis 'a in R^N arbitrary' to a ≠ 0 via 0 < ∑ (a i * K i)^2, which is reduced applicability (recorded under C04 and C11), not extra strength. The per-index parameterisation of the bound (C09) is genuine pointwise strengthening. Each of these is identified and classified.

semantic_checklist.source_evidence: The printed statement excludes nothing: it allows a = 0 and does not exclude all X_i being 0 a.s., in which case K = 0. In both cases the printed right-hand side divides by zero, so the display is not a well-defined real number there (and under the +infinity convention it would assert P <= 0, false at t = 0 since P{|0| >= 0} = 1).
semantic_checklist.lean_evidence: SubExponentialLinearMGF forces 0 < K i, excluding the K = 0 degeneracy; the hypothesis 0 < ∑ i, (a i * K i)^2 excludes a = 0 and, together with K i > 0, also makes Finset.univ.sup' hne (fun i => |a i| * K i) > 0, so neither Lean division ever hits the junk value x / 0 = 0. Finset.sup' is applied with the nonemptiness proof hne, so the maximum is well defined.
semantic_checklist.reasoning: Both degeneracies at which the printed formula is ill-defined are excluded by exactly the minimal hypotheses needed, and no Lean junk value (division by zero, integral of a non-integrable function, sup of an empty family) is exploited to make the statement true for an unintended reason. Boundary values inside the intended domain are kept: t = 0 is admitted (0 ≤ t) and the bound there reads mu.real(...) ≤ 2, which is true and matches the printed 'for every t >= 0'.

semantic_checklist.source_evidence: The printed theorem has nonvacuous content: for large t the right-hand side is far below 1, and the normalized display on printed page 37 exhibits the intended regime.
semantic_checklist.lean_evidence: Hypotheses are satisfiable: take ι = Fin n, Ω a product of n copies of a two-point space with mu the fair product measure and X i the i-th Rademacher coordinate; each is measurable, integrable, mean zero, jointly independent (iIndepFun) and satisfies E exp(lam X i) = cosh lam ≤ exp(lam^2/2) ≤ exp(1^2 lam^2) for all lam, so SubExponentialLinearMGF holds with K i = 1 > 0. Taking a i = 1 gives ∑ (a i * K i)^2 = n > 0, so the added nondegeneracy hypothesis is met.
semantic_checklist.reasoning: The hypothesis set is inhabited in exactly the intended setting, so the statement is not vacuous. The conclusion is not trivially true either: with the above data and t = n the bound reads mu.real{|∑ X i| ≥ n} ≤ 2 exp(-c n), which is a nontrivial assertion (below 1 for n large), so the inequality is not satisfied merely because the right-hand side always exceeds 1 or because a denominator degenerated.

lean_implies_source.reasoning: Assume the target statement with witness c. Let X_1, ..., X_N be independent, mean zero and sub-exponential, let a in R^N and t >= 0, and put K = max_i ||X_i||_psi_1. Non-degenerate case K > 0 and a ≠ 0: by Proposition 2.7.1, printed page 32, property (a)-(d) implies property (e), and by footnote 8 on printed page 36 property (e) holds with a parameter within an absolute constant factor of the psi_1 norm; hence there is an absolute C >= 1 with E exp(lam X_i) <= exp((C K)^2 lam^2) for all |lam| <= 1/(C K), for every i. Instantiate the target with the constant family K i := C K (legal: measurability and integrability come with 'random variable' and 'mean zero'; 0 < C K holds). Then ∑ (a_i K i)^2 = C^2 K^2 ||a||_2^2 > 0, so the added hypothesis holds, and max_i |a_i| K i = C K ||a||_inf. The target therefore gives P{|∑ a_i X_i| >= t} <= 2 exp(-(c) min(t^2/(C^2 K^2 ||a||_2^2), t/(C K ||a||_inf))) <= 2 exp(-(c/C^2) min(t^2/(K^2 ||a||_2^2), t/(K ||a||_inf))), which is the printed bound with the absolute constant c/C^2 > 0, independent of N, the X_i, a and t. Degenerate cases: if a = 0 or K = 0 the printed right-hand side divides by zero and is not a well-defined real number, so nothing is asserted there (and under the reading x/0 = 0 the printed bound becomes the trivially true P <= 2). Hence the target implies the source result.

source_implies_lean.reasoning: Assume Theorem 2.8.2 with absolute constant c_S. Let the target data be given: joint independence, SubExponentialLinearMGF mu (X i) (K i) for each i, 0 < S := ∑ (a i K i)^2, M := max_i |a i| K i, t >= 0. By Proposition 2.7.1 (printed page 32, direction e => b => a-d) there is an absolute C >= 1 with kappa_i := ||X_i||_psi_1 <= C K i for every i. Let J := {i : a i ≠ 0 and kappa_i > 0}. If J is empty then ∑ a_i X_i = 0 a.s. and the target bound holds directly (at t = 0 the right-hand side is 2 >= 1; for t > 0 the left-hand side is 0). Otherwise set s := max_{i in J} |a_i| kappa_i > 0, b_i := |a_i| kappa_i / s ≠ 0 and Y_i := (a_i / b_i) X_i for i in J. Then ||Y_i||_psi_1 = s for all i in J, so K_Y := max_{i in J} ||Y_i||_psi_1 = s, and ∑_J b_i Y_i = ∑_J a_i X_i = ∑_i a_i X_i a.s. The Y_i are independent mean-zero sub-exponential, so Theorem 2.8.2 applied to the family (Y_i)_{i in J} with weight vector (b_i)_{i in J} gives the bound with K_Y^2 ||b||_2^2 = ∑_J (a_i kappa_i)^2 <= C^2 S and K_Y ||b||_inf = max_J |a_i| kappa_i <= C M. Monotonicity of the min and of exp then yields P{|∑ a_i X_i| >= t} <= 2 exp(-(c_S/C^2) min(t^2/S, t/M)), i.e. the target statement with witness c := c_S/C^2 > 0, an absolute constant. So the printed result, being universally quantified over families and weight vectors, absorbs the weights and recovers the per-index form.

findings.source_evidence: Theorem 2.8.2, printed page 37: '... <= 2 exp[- c min( t^2/(K^2||a||_2^2), t/(K||a||_inf) )] where K = max_i ||X_i||_psi_1.' The undebatable shape is a single scalar K multiplied by ||a||_2^2 and by ||a||_inf.
findings.lean_evidence: The target's denominators are ∑ i, (a i * K i)^2 and Finset.univ.sup' hne (fun i => |a i| * K i), with a per-index family K : ι → ℝ. Neither max_i K i, nor ||a||_2, nor ||a||_inf occurs anywhere in the statement.
findings.impact: Pointwise the target is the un-weakened Theorem 2.8.1 applied to a_i X_i (the intermediate step named in the introducing sentence 'let us apply it for a_i X_i instead of X_i'), and its exponent can be arbitrarily larger than the printed one (K = (1, M), a = (1, 1/M): exponent argument min(t^2/2, t) versus min(t^2/M^2, t/M)). As closed ∃c∀-statements the two are inter-derivable (weights can be absorbed into the variables), so faithfulness is preserved, but the derivation of the printed display from this declaration is not a matter of unfolding notation: it needs a rescaling argument plus Proposition 2.7.1. A reader looking for the printed Theorem 2.8.2 in the library would not find its formula here, and Corollary 2.8.3 does not follow by plain instantiation either.

findings.source_evidence: Definition 2.7.5 with (2.21), printed page 33: '||X||_psi_1 = inf{ t > 0 : E exp(|X|/t) <= 2 }', and Theorem 2.8.2's clause 'where K = max_i ||X_i||_psi_1'. Proposition 2.7.1 (e), printed page 32: 'E exp(lam X) <= exp(K_5^2 lam^2) for all lam such that |lam| <= 1/K_5', with footnote 8 on printed page 36 noting that property e holds for a K_5 within an absolute constant factor of ||X||_psi_1.
findings.lean_evidence: SubExponentialLinearMGF mu X K := Measurable X ∧ 0 < K ∧ Integrable X mu ∧ (∫ X = 0) ∧ ∀ lam, |lam| ≤ K⁻¹ → Integrable (fun ω => exp (lam * X ω)) mu ∧ ∫ exp (lam * X) ≤ exp (K^2 * lam^2). The sub-exponential norm itself is never defined or mentioned.
findings.impact: The distributional hypothesis is stated through the source's equivalent property (e) with an explicit parameter, so the hypothesis class is the same only up to an absolute constant factor, absorbed into the existential c. That is legitimate for an absolute-constant theorem and is the very property the book's own proof of 2.8.1 uses, but it means the audited statement does not depend on Definition 2.7.5 at all, so nothing in the formal statement pins K to the psi_1 norm; a later reader must supply Proposition 2.7.1 to connect them.

findings.source_evidence: '... and a = (a_1, ..., a_N) in R^N. Then, for every t >= 0 ...' (printed page 37): a is arbitrary, with no nonvanishing condition, and the printed statement asserts the bound for every such a.

This is a necessary repair rather than a substantive loss, because at a = 0 the printed right-hand side divides by zero (and under the +infinity convention would falsely assert P <= 0 at t = 0), so no content of the printed theorem is lost; but the printed universality in a is not literally reproduced.

rationale:
The printed result (PDF page 26, printed page 37) is: there is an absolute c > 0 such that for independent mean-zero sub-exponential X_1, ..., X_N, any a in R^N and any t >= 0, P{|sum a_i X_i| >= t} <= 2 exp[-c min(t^2/(K^2||a||_2^2), t/(K||a||_inf))] with K = max_i ||X_i||_psi_1. The target reproduces the whole architecture of this statement correctly: an outermost existential absolute constant c > 0 quantified before the index type, the space, the law, the variables, the weights and t; joint independence (iIndepFun) of the untransformed family; mean zero; a two-sided non-strict tail event on the real-valued weighted sum; probability read as mu.real under IsProbabilityMeasure; prefactor exactly 2; a negated product of c with a two-argument min whose sub-gaussian branch comes first; t >= 0 admitted including t = 0. Every routine operator was interpreted from its declaration and checks out (Measure.real = toReal of the measure, GE.ge = flipped ≤, abs = max a (-a), sup' = maximum over a nonempty finset, Min.min = real minimum), and no Lean junk value is being exploited: the two divisions are protected by 0 < ∑ (a i K i)^2 together with K i > 0, and the MGF clause of the local definition carries its own integrability hypotheses rather than relying on the integral of a non-integrable function being 0.

Two real deviations must be recorded. First, the sub-exponential norm of Definition 2.7.5 never appears: the hypothesis is the book's equivalent property (e) of Proposition 2.7.1 with an explicit per-index parameter K i, which by footnote 8 (printed page 36) matches ||X_i||_psi_1 only up to an absolute constant factor. Second, and more visibly, the bound's denominators are ∑ (a i K i)^2 and max_i |a i| K i, i.e. Theorem 2.8.1's shape applied to the variables a_i X_i, rather than the printed K^2||a||_2^2 and K||a||_inf; pointwise the target's exponent can be arbitrarily larger than the printed one. A third, minor deviation is the added nondegeneracy hypothesis 0 < ∑ (a i K i)^2, i.e. a ≠ 0, which repairs the printed division by zero at a = 0.

Judged as closed propositions, both implications nevertheless hold with absolute constants. Target implies source: instantiate the per-index family with the constant C * max_i ||X_i||_psi_1 supplied by Proposition 2.7.1, which turns the two target denominators into exactly C^2 K^2||a||_2^2 and C K ||a||_inf and yields the printed bound with constant c/C^2. Source implies target: since the printed theorem is universally quantified over families and weight vectors, apply it to the rescaled variables Y_i = (a_i/b_i) X_i with b_i = |a_i| ||X_i||_psi_1 / s, which equalizes the psi_1 norms and converts K_Y^2||b||_2^2 and K_Y||b||_inf into ∑ (a_i ||X_i||_psi_1)^2 and max_i |a_i| ||X_i||_psi_1, within a constant factor of the target's denominators; degenerate index sets are handled separately. Both directions therefore hold, and the classification derived from yes/yes is faithful-equivalent, hence accepted = true.

I nonetheless set requires_adjudication = true, and marked C04, C06 and C09 as failures, because the equivalence is not readable off the declaration: the target displays the pre-weakening Theorem 2.8.1 form, omits all three carrying notations of the printed statement (||X||_psi_1, ||a||_2, ||a||_inf) and adds a side condition, so recovering the printed Theorem 2.8.2 (or Corollary 2.8.3 by the a_i = 1/N specialization) requires Proposition 2.7.1 plus a rescaling argument rather than mere unfolding. Whether a module claiming to formalize Theorem 2.8.2 may state the strictly finer 2.8.1-applied form instead of the printed display, and may parameterize by the property-(e) constant rather than the psi_1 norm, is a policy question for the adjudicator; the statement is satisfiable and nonvacuous (independent Rademacher variables with K i = 1, a i = 1 satisfy every hypothesis and give a nontrivial bound at t = n).
